hero.headline: DeSantis vetoes sovereign immunity bill that raised caps on government negligence payouts
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis rejected legislation that would have increased damage caps for people harmed by government negligence for the first time in 16 years. The bill passed with strong bipartisan support in March before DeSantis vetoed it, saying that raising the caps would encourage more frivolous lawsuits. "When you raise the cap, you are going to generate more unmeritorious lawsuits," he said. The measure would have increased sovereign immunity caps from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 per person and $500,000 per incident, effective October 1.

HB 145, sponsored by Sarasota Republican Rep. Fiona McFarland with a Senate companion bill from Lake Mary Republican Sen. Jason Brodeur, faced fierce opposition from more than 240 lobbyists representing counties, cities and their agencies, including public hospitals. These government entities worried about budget shortfalls under a proposed property tax amendment. The bill would have allowed local governments to voluntarily settle claims exceeding the new caps without requiring legislative approval. The original proposal included higher caps of $500,000 per person and $1 million per incident, which were reduced in a last-minute compromise. Sovereign immunity is a centuries-old legal standard that shields state and local governments from settling lawsuits without their consent. Currently, victims seeking compensation above the caps must obtain approval through special claims bills passed by the Legislature.

McFarland has argued that the current system creates unequal protection under the law. She contends that harmed individuals face an "incredibly arduous and difficult process" with vastly different outcomes depending on whether the responsible party is a public or private entity. "If you or I or one of our loved ones is hit by a truck, we have to pay attention to what's on the side of that truck," she said. "Depending on whether there's a corporate logo or a government seal, we have different access to monetary wholeness." State lawmakers consider roughly a dozen claims bills annually benefiting people injured through government carelessness or wrongly incarcerated exonerees. This year, just over one-third of 14 such measures passed both chambers, including cases involving a man paralyzed in a police van, a motorist injured in a crash with a state tractor, and a young girl hurt due to Department of Children and Families negligence.

DeSantis defended his veto by noting the current system works because some claims bills clear the Legislature yearly. "I signed a number of claims bills this year," he said. "People have gotten millions of dollars with that." However, the Florida Justice Association criticized the veto as a gift to insurance companies and a disservice to Florida families. The group noted that under the current system, victims often wait years or over a decade for compensation. McFarland and Brodeur, both seeking reelection, have not indicated whether they will refile the legislation for the 2027 session.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd seeks to keep Paula Stark off ballot after filing deadline dispute
cards.teaser: Five state employees dispute St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark's account of a paperwork mix-up that left her disqualified from the ballot less than 30 minutes before the June 12 deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep Republican Paula Stark off the ballot for House District 47, disputing her claims that a paperwork mix-up disqualified her candidacy. Five state employees submitted sworn declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the required Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted remaining paperwork in the final hour before the June 12 noon deadline. Stark's incomplete materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the deadline. Election Records Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve noted in a court declaration that three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still had not submitted the Form 6. Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who failed to properly submit a Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and still qualified.

Reeve documented Stark's history of paperwork problems, including filing a campaign finance report over one month late, reporting excessive contributions, and maintaining an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 will open to all voters deciding between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves, as no other Republican filed for the traditionally blue seat covering parts of Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd noted ballots must be mailed to overseas military members and their families by July 4.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach was recognized as one of just 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where city leaders presented efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying Riviera Beach earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize the city and improve quality of life for residents. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said.

City leaders say the recognition reflects years of work focused on improving civic health, strengthening trust between residents and local government, and creating opportunities for the community to play a direct role in shaping the city's future. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award is a tribute to their heart and determination. Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Let Late Lead Slip Away in 10-3 Loss to Tarpons
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover P
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park.

Tampa scored six unearned runs in the eighth inning, capitalizing on four Mets errors, then added three more runs in the ninth to pull away on Independence Day. The Tarpons extended their winning streak to eight games, while St. Lucie dropped its ninth straight.

The Mets led 3-1 entering the eighth after building the advantage with timely offense and strong relief work. But Tampa's comeback began after Hans Montero reached and eventually scored the tying run when Bryce Martin-Grudzielanek hit a two-out ground ball to third baseman Branny De Oleo. The ball deflected off De Oleo's glove for an error, allowing Montero to come home and even the game at 3-3.

The inning continued from there, and David McCann delivered the decisive blow with a three-run home run off Conner Ware to give Tampa a 6-3 lead. McCann struck again in the ninth, launching another three-run homer off Luis Alvarez to make it 10-3.

McCann finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk and seven RBI. The performance came one day after he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.

St. Lucie had trailed 1-0 early before tying the game in the fourth inning on an RBI groundout by Simon Juan. Chase Meggers gave the Mets a 2-1 lead in the fifth with a two-out RBI single against Tyler Boudreau. Juan then added a solo home run off Boudreau in the sixth to stretch the lead to 3-1.

Ware had kept Tampa quiet through three scoreless innings before the eighth-inning unraveling. He took the loss after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings, though all five were unearned.

Tampa reliever Jose M. Rodriguez earned the win after pitching a perfect seventh inning.

The Mets fell to 2-10 in the second half and 35-43 overall. Tampa improved to 11-3 in the second half and 46-34 overall.

The teams close their six-game series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m. It will be Little League Day. Little leaguers who wear their jerseys will receive free admission and a gift courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ruling allows absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day to count if received later
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, preserving grace period laws that election officials depend on.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward. The ruling preserves grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots. The case, Republican National Committee v. Wetzel, centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count, provided they bear an Election Day postmark.

A panel of three Trump-appointed Fifth Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day. The Supreme Court reversed that ruling. Justice Amy Coney Barrett, a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice Roberts and the three liberal justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. The election-day statutes say nothing about ballot receipt, she wrote, and the court cannot add to the words Congress chose. States retain authority to set their own receipt deadlines, meaning grace period laws in roughly 30 states covering military and overseas voters are also protected.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating in state report card
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County schools earned a third consecutive A rating from the state, with S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach making a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, with 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, receiving either an "A" or "B" grade this year. That represents an increase from 120 schools with those top ratings in the previous year. The district also achieved a record graduation rate of 93.5%, and 86% of seniors completed at least one college-level course through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge AICE, or Dual Enrollment programs. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach experienced a dramatic turnaround, jumping from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years in that role after five years as assistant principal, credited the improvement to curriculum changes that began three years ago. The school modified its early childhood program, which serves students starting at age 3 through kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. Spady was one of four district schools to make the jump from a "C" to an "A" this year. The other three schools include Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation attracts international artists to Fort Pierce with residency program
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and international artists through its residency program.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation, housed in the historic Crain Estate, preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain in Fort Pierce. Mr. Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The estate retains approximately 90 percent of its original character, including the smoking and bourbon room with man paneling and prestained glass that leads to a bar on the front patio. The Crains traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items including a gazebo shipped from India. Guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture are available every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Art director Krystal Masters said the foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character without commercializing it.

The Peacock House gets its name from birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced seven peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, and the flock has grown to over 100. Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognized by his limp, is a beloved bird with his own bowls and a daily hand-feeding routine. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts international artists with simple but elegant accommodations. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including one-on-one instruction in sculpting and watercolor designed for complete beginners.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year, with ground beef and strawberries showing biggest increases
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
The American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey found that a Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said shoppers should compare stores to see who has the best deals for groceries on their list. Woroch said the biggest thing for families is cutting down food waste, and that begins with a meal plan.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road as widening project continues
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to the Florida Turnpike.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to the Florida Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie and the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

The partial interchange for the Turnpike is still in the design phase according to the FDOT website. Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said the construction can be annoying but believes it is necessary and that the expanded road will make it easier to get to work. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, July 1, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1 in the Intracoastal Waterway. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies said they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. The sheriff's office said the incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call," the sheriff's office stated in a Facebook post.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire as community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark stating that Misty had passed away in the fire.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described the scene as completely a state of devastation. She reflected on her friendship with White, saying Misty was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, playing the piano, kids and people. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his one and only child Jacob tragically. White's death adds another layer of heartbreak because her birthday is the Fourth of July, so she passed just a few days before turning another year older. Fenn said White has always been a good soul and will always be in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Anthem denies breast cancer reconstruction surgery hours before procedure for Treasure Coast patient
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, recently diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma, had her insurance company deny coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health."

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction, making it an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives her patients the least amount of complications. Last year, after investigative reporting by Katie LaGrone and Matthew Apthorp, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem responded to Clark's denial by stating it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with treatment standards, adding that without FDA approval, the mesh does not meet their coverage standards. Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh more than a week ago thanks to Billington finding a mechanism to make it happen.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes July 6 for $3 million renovation to nearly double slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the facility's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The upgrades include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the improvements serve multiple purposes. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said, noting that the year-long closure will be worthwhile.

Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates from the dock, initially faced uncertainty about continuing operations during the renovation. The city worked out a solution allowing the business to function throughout construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, explained that the city is permitting them to build a gate at the end of the downtown dock's non-floating section for passenger boarding. Kuyrkendall emphasized the dock's importance to the city, stating "Stuart is not Stuart without the water." He acknowledged current limitations during peak times, particularly on weekends, and welcomed the modernization. "Modernizing and expanding this back dock is really going to be great for the city but also for us as well," Kuyrkendall said.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles match with Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her Wimbledon doubles match with sister Venus on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old lost to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 on Tuesday. In an Instagram post, Serena said she was "heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles," noting that coming back to compete and playing alongside Venus "meant the world to me." She explained that while she "did everything I could," her knee "just isn't ready to compete." The post included images of four syringes containing fluid drained from her knee after the singles match, along with a video showing her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her.

The Williams sisters, with Venus at age 46, were scheduled to face Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in a first-round doubles match that had been pushed back to allow Serena more recovery time. However, Serena hinted at a potential return, saying "stay tuned to a city near you" as the U.S. Open approaches. Venus competed in mixed doubles on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters are six-time Wimbledon women's doubles champions.

cards.headline: Argentina survives scare from Cape Verde 3-2 to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday and advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 in a thrilling match in which the tiny island nation challenged the reigning champion until the final minutes of extra time.
cards.body:
The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Messi scored early in regulation, his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd to put Argentina ahead 2-1. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde, both equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.

Messi added another brilliant goal to his resume, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Martinez lofted a pass toward him, taking a quick touch and hammering a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead in the 29th minute. The Argentina captain has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbapp in the Golden Boot race as the top scorer in this year's World Cup, and extended his World Cup record, moving two goals ahead of Mbapp on the all-time list.

Argentina advanced to face Egypt, which beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday, in Atlanta on Tuesday. Cape Verde's memorable World Cup debut had been a stunning run that few outside the tiny island nation off the western coast of Africa could have predicted, with the team securing surprising draws against Spain and Uruguay and another against Saudi Arabia.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football eyes state title run after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are setting their sights on a state title as they prepare for the 2026 fall football season following a 10-2 record and district championship last year. A second-round playoff exit has motivated the program to push further. Head coach Jimmy Robertson credits the veteran senior class as the foundation for potential success. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To compete at a higher level, Saint Andrew's has constructed a more demanding nonconference schedule. Senior quarterback Jack Williams explained the reasoning: "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people." For the Scots, improvement is measured by playoff advancement. Senior Jack Whelche stated: "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs."

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Season Programs Through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. During nesting season, Loggerhead Marinelife Center's education and research departments work together to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups encourage beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach Country Club Hosts Fourth of July Fireworks and Pool Party
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors celebrated Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event included a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers said this years event also recognized Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities began with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests enjoyed a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families took part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign began around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course offered one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse also hosted a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: DeSantis vetoes sovereign immunity bill that raised caps on government negligence payouts
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis rejected legislation that would have increased damage caps for people harmed by government negligence for the first time in 16 years. The bill passed with strong bipartisan support in March before DeSantis vetoed it, saying that raising the caps would encourage more frivolous lawsuits. "When you raise the cap, you are going to generate more unmeritorious lawsuits," he said. The measure would have increased sovereign immunity caps from $200,000 per person and $300,000 per incident to $350,000 per person and $500,000 per incident, effective October 1.

HB 145, sponsored by Sarasota Republican Rep. Fiona McFarland with a Senate companion bill from Lake Mary Republican Sen. Jason Brodeur, faced fierce opposition from more than 240 lobbyists representing counties, cities and their agencies, including public hospitals. These government entities worried about budget shortfalls under a proposed property tax amendment. The bill would have allowed local governments to voluntarily settle claims exceeding the new caps without requiring legislative approval. The original proposal included higher caps of $500,000 per person and $1 million per incident, which were reduced in a last-minute compromise. Sovereign immunity is a centuries-old legal standard that shields state and local governments from settling lawsuits without their consent. Currently, victims seeking compensation above the caps must obtain approval through special claims bills passed by the Legislature.

McFarland has argued that the current system creates unequal protection under the law. She contends that harmed individuals face an "incredibly arduous and difficult process" with vastly different outcomes depending on whether the responsible party is a public or private entity. "If you or I or one of our loved ones is hit by a truck, we have to pay attention to what's on the side of that truck," she said. "Depending on whether there's a corporate logo or a government seal, we have different access to monetary wholeness." State lawmakers consider roughly a dozen claims bills annually benefiting people injured through government carelessness or wrongly incarcerated exonerees. This year, just over one-third of 14 such measures passed both chambers, including cases involving a man paralyzed in a police van, a motorist injured in a crash with a state tractor, and a young girl hurt due to Department of Children and Families negligence.

DeSantis defended his veto by noting the current system works because some claims bills clear the Legislature yearly. "I signed a number of claims bills this year," he said. "People have gotten millions of dollars with that." However, the Florida Justice Association criticized the veto as a gift to insurance companies and a disservice to Florida families. The group noted that under the current system, victims often wait years or over a decade for compensation. McFarland and Brodeur, both seeking reelection, have not indicated whether they will refile the legislation for the 2027 session.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd seeks to keep Paula Stark off ballot after filing deadline dispute
cards.teaser: Five state employees dispute St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark's account of a paperwork mix-up that left her disqualified from the ballot less than 30 minutes before the June 12 deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep Republican Paula Stark off the ballot for House District 47, disputing her claims that a paperwork mix-up disqualified her candidacy. Five state employees submitted sworn declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the required Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests, and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted remaining paperwork in the final hour before the June 12 noon deadline. Stark's incomplete materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the deadline. Election Records Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve noted in a court declaration that three weeks after the qualifying deadline, Stark still had not submitted the Form 6. Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who failed to properly submit a Form 6, but half of them corrected the problems and still qualified.

Reeve documented Stark's history of paperwork problems, including filing a campaign finance report over one month late, reporting excessive contributions, and maintaining an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over $16,000 in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 will open to all voters deciding between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves, as no other Republican filed for the traditionally blue seat covering parts of Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd noted ballots must be mailed to overseas military members and their families by July 4.

cards.headline: United States men's soccer team faces Belgium in World Cup knockout round Monday
cards.teaser: The U.S. team earned its first knockout stage victory since 2002 with a 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina on Wednesday, but will be without Folarin Balogun against Belgium after a red card.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002, dispatching Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night while playing the final 36 minutes with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded on what coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly was never a red card. Longtime Premier League VAR referee Andy Davies called the decision wrong, telling ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession of the ball in a normal football movement. Pochettino pointed out that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing. Weston McKennie spoke for the locker room: "I think it's a bit bogus."

Balogun, one of their top players, will watch Monday from the bench against a Belgian side that earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S. since the inaugural 1930 World Cup, the lone American victory in the head-to-head. The team won Wednesday without Balogun for the better part of an hour. The Americans are well-coached, physically capable, and playing at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ruling allows absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day to count if received later
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, preserving grace period laws that election officials depend on.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward. The ruling preserves grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots. The case, Republican National Committee v. Wetzel, centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count, provided they bear an Election Day postmark.

A panel of three Trump-appointed Fifth Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day. The Supreme Court reversed that ruling. Justice Amy Coney Barrett, a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice Roberts and the three liberal justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. The election-day statutes say nothing about ballot receipt, she wrote, and the court cannot add to the words Congress chose. States retain authority to set their own receipt deadlines, meaning grace period laws in roughly 30 states covering military and overseas voters are also protected.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms historic Fort Pierce estate into artistic destination with global artists
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as a vibrant artistic hub by transforming the historic Crain Estate into a cultural center that welcomes both local and international artists. The nonprofit organization honors the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, former residents of the property whose personal touches remain visible throughout the facility. Jaxson Crain's trade as a tile worker is evident in his craftsmanship, which covers floors, walls, and ceilings. According to Krystal Masters, the art director, the estate has retained approximately 90 percent of its original character since the Crains lived there. The foundation has deliberately avoided commercializing the space, choosing instead to preserve its authentic residential charm. Visitors can experience the estate's lush gardens and distinctive architecture through guided tours offered every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Crains were world travelers who visited nine times and filled their Florida home with unique treasures from around the globe. Among their most notable acquisitions was a gazebo shipped from India, which features small peacock details painted into its design. The estate's distinctive smoking and bourbon room reflects the era with wood paneling and a bathroom decorated in masculine tones. A pristine stained glass window connects this room to a bar on the front patio. The foundation's commitment to preservation means these spaces remain largely unchanged from their original condition.

The property takes its name from the peacocks that have inhabited it for decades. The Crains introduced seven peacocks to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, and the population has since grown to over 100 birds. Among them is Bob, a beloved peacock believed to be 60 years old and recognizable by his distinctive limp. Bob receives special treatment at the estate, complete with his own feeding bowls and daily hand-feeding by staff. Tour guides highlight the memorable moments when children feed peacocks directly from their hands. The estate's animal history also includes a colorful anecdote about a baby monkey that Jaxson Crain reportedly brought home from South America, smuggling it in his pocket.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that attracts creators from around the world, providing simple yet elegant accommodations on the grounds. The on-site art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with Masters leading one-on-one sessions tailored for complete beginners. Students work with various mediums including sculpting and watercolor painting, often completing finished pieces during their first class. "The majority of my classes are one on one classes you come in with zero experience and you walk out with a piece of art and it makes you feel good," Masters explains. For her, art serves as therapeutic practice that helps people destress and disconnect from digital distractions.
